title: The Open Current
premise: Hazel Almeida, a salvage diver scraping a living off a wreck the navy refuses to acknowledge, is hired by a dying prospector who trades him a map to a sunken river valley in exchange for one promise: bring the expedition home, and tell no one what it finds. As Hazel assembles a ragtag crew of divers, engineers, and a cartographer with her own debts, the concession clock ticks down and the navy's interest sharpens from rumor to surveillance. The expedition uncovers a pre-war settlement whose flooded archives hold records that could rewrite the region's history—and implicate the very institution that sank it. In the end, Hazel keeps half his promise: he brings everyone home alive, but releases the truth anonymously, sacrificing his invisibility and his salvage claim to save his found family.
about_author: Bram Joubert is the pen name of a former commercial diver turned novelist who spent six years working salvage contracts off three continents. He writes adventure fiction about people whose livelihoods depend on knowing exactly what the water takes and what it gives back.

chapters.title: Cold Water Rules
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A routine salvage dive on the navy-sealed wreck goes wrong when Hazel spots a sealed compartment the official manifests say doesn't exist. He surfaces with questions instead of cargo. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a man who survives by not asking.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Prospector Elias Vann tracks Hazel down at a dockside bar, coughing blood, offering a hand-drawn map of a drowned river valley in exchange for a promise: take an expedition there, bring them back, tell no one what they find. Emotional beat: temptation wrapped in obligation.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Elias dies before dawn, leaving Hazel the map, a battered dive log, and a legal-looking concession permit expiring in ninety days. Hazel realizes accepting makes him custodian of something dangerous. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger who trusted him.

chapters.title: Assembling the Impossible
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel recruits engineer Tomas Reyes, broke and brilliant; deckhand June Okafor, who owes dangerous money; and cartographer Marguerite Chen, who recognizes the valley's coordinates and lies about why. Emotional beat: cautious hope as strangers become a crew.

chapters.title: The Navy's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A naval officer, Commander Locke, visits Marguerite's office asking pointed questions about survey requests near the valley. She deflects but understands someone else has the map's scent. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Departure on Borrowed Money
chapters.summary: June's POV. The crew loads the aging salvage vessel Kestrel with borrowed equipment and June's quietly desperate financing. Hazel lays down rules: no radio chatter about destination, no promises beyond return. Emotional beat: the fragile thrill of setting out.

chapters.title: First Blood in the Channel
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A storm forces the Kestrel into an unplanned anchorage where a patrol boat boards them, all courtesy and veiled threat. Locke's name appears on the boarding papers. Emotional beat: the crew learning they are already being watched.

chapters.title: The Valley That Isn't on Charts
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They reach the mapped gorge and find the river dammed and drowned decades ago—by no public project. Sonar reveals structures beneath. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Descent to the Rooftops
chapters.summary: Hazel and Tomas dive the flooded town, swimming streets between rooftops, finding a church bell and a municipal seal predating any record. Hazel pockets a corroded document tube. Emotional beat: wonder, and the first taste of the secret's weight.

chapters.title: What the Archive Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The recovered documents reveal the settlement was deliberately flooded—residents relocated under coercion—to bury evidence of a catastrophic engineering failure the government blamed elsewhere. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; history as crime scene.

chapters.title: June's Creditors Surface
chapters.summary: June's POV. A supply launch arrives carrying not fuel but one of June's debt collectors, offering to forgive everything if she reports the expedition's findings to interested parties. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by survival math.

chapters.title: The Turned Radio
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The Kestrel's radio transmits during a scheduled silence window. Someone aboard is signaling—or was made to. Suspicion fractures the crew over dinner. Emotional beat: trust cracking under pressure.

chapters.title: Locke Comes Upstream
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Commander Locke arrives by helicopter with a seizure order citing national security, offering Hazel salvage rights and quiet money in exchange for the documents and silence. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit and personal.

chapters.title: Ninety Days Becomes Nine
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite discovers the concession permit's fine print: unexplored claims void at expiry unless physically documented on site. They have nine days to finish or lose everything—including leverage. Emotional beat: desperation converted into focus.

chapters.title: The Deep Archive Dive
chapters.summary: Hazel and Tomas's alternating POV. A push past safe depth limits reaches the flooded records office. Tomas takes a decompression hit; Hazel drags him up through a collapsing stairwell. Emotional beat: brotherhood forged in nitrogen and terror.

chapters.title: Chamber Pressure
chapters.summary: June's POV. With Tomas in a makeshift decompression rig and supplies failing, June confesses her deal with the collector to Hazel—not to betray them, but because she refused to sign. Emotional beat: shame transformed into earned belonging.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Narrows
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Leaving the valley, the Kestrel is boxed in by two patrol boats. Hazel runs the narrows at flood tide—a maneuver that should kill them—and loses the pursuers in whitewater. Emotional beat: reckless courage as love language.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Storm-bound in a cove, the crew debates: sell the archive to Locke, bury it, or publish. Each argues from their own wound. Hazel finally tells them Elias's promise—and admits he intends to keep only half of it. Emotional beat: the found family choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: The Handover That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel meets Locke alone to trade copies for the charges against June and Tomas to be dropped—but hands over doctored scans, keeping originals hidden in the wreck compartment from chapter one. Emotional beat: the diver's oldest skill, holding breath while lying.

chapters.title: Expiry
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. On the final day of the concession, the crew files complete documentation from international waters via a journalist Marguerite trusts, then scatters the physical archive across three countries. Emotional beat: ticking-clock release, terror and exhilaration fused.

chapters.title: The Story Breaks
chapters.summary: June's POV. The publication detonates: hearings announced, Locke suspended, the drowned town's survivors' descendants given standing. June's debts evaporate under sudden notoriety. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by loss of the anonymous life they all valued.

chapters.title: Open Current
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Months later, Hazel dives the old navy wreck one last time—now an open investigation site—and retrieves nothing, needing nothing. The crew reunites aboard the Kestrel for a new contract, chosen this time. Emotional beat: peace earned; memory kept, finally shareable.
